title: Inclusionary zoning direction and Growing Together engagement
subtitle: Also covered: a 127-unit townhouse subdivision on New Dundee Road and a condominium approval on Benninger Drive.
overview: The committee's main item was the proposed approach to inclusionary zoning, which would require some affordable rental units in new developments near Ion transit stations. The committee recommended that staff, working with Waterloo, Cambridge and the Region, consult further and draft official plan and zoning changes for Council {{vote:m2}}. Staff expect to return with those documents in December. The proposal would apply to developments of 50 units or more and phase in set-aside rates over time. Staff estimated it would deliver about 27 units a year under current market conditions.

The committee also recommended that staff use community input from the Growing Together workshops to inform planning rules for the major transit station areas {{vote:m3}}. It recommended draft approval and rezoning for a 127-unit townhouse development at 1000 New Dundee Road, which would also place a protected wetland in public ownership {{vote:m4}}. It also recommended draft condominium approval for 630 and 690 Benninger Drive {{vote:m1}}.
These are recommendations. Council will consider them at a later meeting.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that staff consult further with industry, housing providers and the public, then draft an Inclusionary Zoning official plan policy and zoning amendments for Council, in coordination with Waterloo, Cambridge and the Region {{vote:m2}}.
The committee recommended that staff use the community input from the Growing Together workshops to inform continued work on planning for the major transit station areas.

decisions.item: 1000 New Dundee Road subdivision and rezoning
decisions.detail: The committee recommended draft plan of subdivision approval and a zoning change to allow a townhouse development, with the wetland area conveyed to the City.
The committee recommended draft approval of the condominium application for 630 and 690 Benninger Drive, subject to staff conditions.

debate: Staff said the inclusionary zoning policy balances affordable housing against housing supply, given high construction costs and interest rates. They said the 50-unit threshold avoids burdening missing-middle buildings, and that set-aside rates start low and rise over time, with reviews every two years.

A delegate urged applying the policy to buildings of 10 units or more, with no ramp-up, in all station areas, and asked for a low-rise zone beyond the current boundaries. Staff said the boundaries are already approved and in force. One councillor asked staff to revisit the 50-unit threshold and begin at 5%, citing the long affordable housing waiting list. Others supported the staff approach and cautioned against stifling supply.

Several councillors called 27 units a year low but said it reflects current market conditions and can rise. Some asked about additional incentives, more collaboration with universities, and more rental and income-geared housing.

On Growing Together, a delegate said parkland was missing from the workshop exercise and that the downtown has a parkland shortfall. Staff said the exercise tested where building types might go, and they are working with parks staff on a separate project. Councillors praised the hands-on format as engaging.

On New Dundee Road, a councillor was concerned that one entrance would serve 127 units. Staff said a traffic study found one access appropriate for visibility reasons, with a second emergency-only access. Another councillor raised the lack of nearby transit, sidewalks and bike lanes, and staff said Regional improvements are planned.
